rationale: bisort is a small, pointer-heavy Olden benchmark built around recursive tree traversal and a bitonic merge that relies heavily on bitwise arithmetic, so SUB gets the strongest weights: it obfuscates exactly the arithmetic/logic idioms that dominate this code at near-zero runtime and size cost, and its transformations are semantics-preserving on integer/bitwise ops (high CorrectnessRisk tolerance). FLA is weighted next-highest on security because flattening the recursive sort/merge control flow substantially raises reversing effort, but its RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are held moderate and CorrectnessRisk moderate (0.60) since aggressive flattening interacts with the loop/recursion structure that defines bisort's behavior. BCF offers good deterrence but is the worst pass for cost on a tight benchmark like this (classic BCF roughly doubles block counts), so its cost weights are kept low while security stays decent. IBR gets mid-range weights as a complementary control-flow diversifier with acceptable cost; ICALL is kept as a light diversifier (bisort has few indirect-call sites, so features will naturally limit its application) with conservative cost weights. SPLIT and IGV are effectively de-prioritized: SPLIT adds little to already-small functions and IGV has almost no global-variable surface in bisort, so both get low benefit weights but high cost/risk tolerance so they only fire where clearly cheap and safe.
